claim: In the California housing data, median house value is jointly positively associated with median income and average number of rooms per household.
Median house value is negatively associated with average occupancy while accounting for longitude, which shows a positive association with occupancy.
Population size is jointly negatively related to house age and positively related to average occupancy.
Average occupancy increases with longitude and decreases with latitude, reflecting the strong inverse relationship between latitude and longitude.
Average number of rooms per household rises with median income, even after accounting for the negative association between median income and average bedrooms.
Median house value is positively associated with median income and negatively associated with average occupancy when both factors are considered together.
Average occupancy is positively associated with both population size and longitude.
House age is negatively associated with both population size and average number of rooms per household.
Latitude and longitude are strongly negatively linearly correlated.
Median income is positively monotonic associated with median house value.
Median income is positively monotonic associated with average number of rooms per household.
House age is negatively monotonic associated with population size.
Average occupancy is negatively monotonic associated with median house value.
Average number of rooms per household is positively monotonic associated with median house value.
Median income is negatively monotonic associated with average number of bedrooms per household.
